question: True or false: past a warming threshold, the Greenland ice sheet could keep shrinking even if warming stopped there?
answer: True. As the ice thins, its surface sinks into lower, warmer air, so it melts faster still. Robinson and colleagues modelled a threshold between 0.8 and 3.2°C of global warming, best estimate 1.6°C, beyond which the sheet heads towards loss. It would take thousands of years, but it would not readily grow back.
move: Some damage keeps going after the push stops; find the threshold first.
ask: Which slide in my life would keep going even if I stopped what started it?
trap: Stop the warming and the ice should simply stop melting too.
source: Robinson et al., Nature Climate Change, 2012
reference: Robinson, Calov & Ganopolski, Multistability and critical thresholds of the Greenland ice sheet, Nature Climate Change, 2012
